_comment: SYNTHETIC — hand-built from the documented response shapes in Yahoo's official
Fantasy Sports API guide and from published wrapper-library samples (yfpy,
yahoo_fantasy_api). NOT a live capture. Yahoo API access is gated behind an
approval application and NO live call has ever been made from this repo.
Replace with a real redacted capture once API access is approved.
AUTHORED 2026-08-11 (not captured on any date).
MODELS: GET /fantasy/v2/league/461.l.590044/teams?format=json for a league
with exactly ONE team in it (a league mid-fill, which is the natural
way to produce a one-element collection).
REDACTION: all identifiers invented; the manager guid is FAKEGUID...0001.
WHY THIS IS COMMITTED — THE SINGLE-ELEMENT COLLAPSE. A Yahoo collection of N
things is an OBJECT keyed "0","1",... with a sibling "count":
"teams": {"0": {"team": [...]}, "count": 1}      ← the normal one-item form
but a collection with exactly ONE element sometimes collapses to the bare
object instead, with NO numeric key and NO count at all:
"teams": {"team": [...]}                          ← what this file has
Code that walks node["0"] finds nothing and reports an empty league. Code
that iterates the object's keys hits the string "team" where it expected a
numeric index. Either way the result is ZERO ROWS AND NO EXCEPTION, which is
the failure mode this whole pipeline is built to refuse. iter_collection()
handles it by detecting a non-numeric key and yielding the object itself as
the sole element.
THREE COLLAPSES, NESTED, IN ONE PAYLOAD — this is not a contrived stack; it
is what a one-team league genuinely looks like:
1. teams       → collapsed to {"team": [...]}          (1 team)
2. team_logos  → collapsed to {"team_logo": {...}}      (1 logo)
3. managers    → collapsed to {"manager": {...}}        (1 manager)
Correct parsing yields exactly 1 team, 1 team-season-state row, 1 manager and
1 team↔manager link. Any of the three mishandled yields 0 for that table
while the others still populate — a partial result that looks like data.
⚠️ THE COUNT KEY IS ABSENT, and its absence is the tell. Anything that
trusts 'count' to size a collection must cope with it not being there;
collection_count() returns None rather than 0, because 'the provider did not
declare a count' is not 'the provider declared zero'.
OTHER PLACES THIS SAME COLLAPSE SHOWS UP (all reachable from this fixture
set): eligible_positions and bye_weeks on a player — see the kicker and the
team defense in yahoo_roster_week.json and yahoo_players_page1.json — and
transaction_data on a trade, which is the reverse trap: there the
SINGLE-ELEMENT case is the LIST form. Every plural thing goes through
as_list(); none of them may be indexed directly.
SHAPE HAZARDS DELIBERATELY PRESENT BEYOND THE COLLAPSE:
1. 'team' is an ARRAY whose element 0 is an ARRAY of single-key dicts.
2. waiver_priority is a bare INT while number_of_moves is the STRING "0"
and number_of_trades is the INT 0 — three ways to say a small number in
one object.
3. roster_adds is a sub-object whose 'coverage_value' is the week number
and whose 'value' is the count — two different meanings, similar names.
4. The manager is the authenticating user (is_owned_by_current_login 1,
is_commissioner "1"), which is exactly the case where a real capture
would also contain an EMAIL. The parser deliberately never reads it and
there is none here.
5. draft_grade / has_draft_grade are absent (predraft league) rather than
empty.
NOT TRUNCATED: a one-team league is one team. The collapse IS the fixture —
adding a second team would destroy it.
